Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today, through the eyes of the Search Engine Roundtable and other search forums on the web.

Google is testing hotel bookings directly in Google Search through a Continue on Google button. Google is testing emojis in the What people are saying section. Google discontinued its Data Feed validation tool. Google image search results now let you click a Google Lens button, which takes you into an AI Overview follow-up query or even an AI Mode follow-up query. Google AdSense is unifying some of its policies into the AdSense for Search publishers policy.

Google Search What People Are Saying AI-Generated Emojis
Google seems to be placing emojis in the AI-generated "What people are saying" box in Google Search. Google does show emojis in its search results, but these emojis are not coming from the website it is referencing, but rather from Google Search and its AI-generated descriptions.

Google Hotel Search Listings With Continue On Google To Book
Google seems to be rolling out hotel booking directly on Google in Google Search but through AI Mode. So when you search on Google and Google shows you the hotels, you can now click on a button that says "Continue on Google" and it then takes you through the AI Mode hotel booking feature to book using your Google account.

Google Search Tests "Show Original Results" Button
Google Search is testing a new button in the search results named "Show original results." It seems this button does something similar to the "Search instead for" link, where Google will auto correct or adapt your query when it thinks you have a typo in your query or you meant to search for something else.

Google Data Feed Validation Tool Has Been Turned Down
Google has "turned down" its Data Feed validation tool and has removed references to it from the Book actions (Book) structured data help documentation. I am not sure when this tool surfaced but likely sometime between October 2016 and December 2017 alongside the broader Actions on Google developer platform.

Google Images Results With Lens To AI Mode Feature
Google image search results now let you click a Google Lens button, which takes you into an AI Overview follow-up query or even an AI Mode follow-up query. This is different from when Google added the Google Lens button to image search results.

Google AdSense Unifying Policies Into AdSense For Search Publishers Policy
Google announced it will update and merge the AdSense for Search (AFS) policies and Search ads policies into a single, unified policy set for AdSense for Search publishers. This will happen on January 17, 2027. Google posted a copy of the new, unified policy.

Branded Google Jenga Game
We have seen Google's custom branded Jenga game set before but here it is again, many years later. I am not sure if this is a new one or an old one but hey, I found it on Instagram the other day.
